prompt:
Cinematic key art for a prestige strategy game, 16:9. A large table map of greater Houston built from layered cut paper in bone and pale sage tones, freeways as raised paper ribbons, small brass pins at scattered points joined by fine red-brown thread, a brass loupe and a closed leather notebook at the edge; lit low from one side at night so every paper layer casts a crisp shadow. High three-quarter view, shallow depth, map detail concentrated in the right 60 percent, left 40 percent in shadow. Palette: bottle green shadow, bone paper, brass, one thread color. Photoreal with painterly restraint, fine film grain. No people, no readable text or place names, no logos, no app interfaces.

ART BIBLE: After hours: every plate is an empty, lit place at night or the edge of night, the hour an owner-operator builds the systems. One world: bottle-green shadows (#1C3229 into near-black #0A0F0D), warm practical light (sodium amber, brass lamps, bone highlights #EDE7DB), wet or polished surfaces holding reflections, faint haze. Photoreal with painterly restraint, like the key art of a prestige narrative or driving game; fine film grain; 35mm anamorphic feel, shallow depth of field, low camera. Composition: subject mass in the right 60 percent, the left 40 percent falls into calm deep shadow where type will sit. Never: people, readable text, signage, logos, brand emblems, license plates, screens with UI, neon, lens flares, glow bloom, sci-fi, plastic CGI gloss, oversaturation. Each plate changes only one variable from the set (its place and its single light source); the palette and grade are shared.
